CFML Language Reference: Functions

IsProtected

Checks whether any security context has a rule that protects the given resource (and action). Unlike IsAuthorized, it does not depend on who is logged in.

Category

Authentication functions

Syntax

IsProtected(resourcetype, resourcename [, action ])

Parameters

resourcetype
The kind of resource: Application, CFML, File, DataSource, Component, Collection, CustomTag or UserObject.
resourcename
The name of the resource.
action
Optional action, such as Read or Write.

Returns

YES if the resource is protected, NO otherwise.

Usage

Use it to decide whether a login is needed at all: if IsProtected returns NO, anybody may proceed; if YES, check IsAuthorized. When no security contexts are defined, every resource is unprotected and the function returns NO.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Resource = "Payroll">
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>IsProtected("Application", "#Resource#") = #IsProtected("Application", Resource)#
<P>
<CFIF NOT IsProtected("Application", Resource)>
  The #Resource# application is open to everyone. Come on in.
<CFELSEIF IsAuthorized("Application", Resource)>
  Welcome, #AuthenticatedUser()#.
<CFELSE>
  Sorry, you need to log in to use #Resource#.
</CFIF>
</CFOUTPUT>

See also

IsAuthorized, IsAuthenticated, CFAUTHENTICATE
